nodes.description: Loss of one copy of the proximal BP4-BP5 interval, approximately 600 kb, between homologous low-copy repeats.

evidence.snippet: The recurrent ~600 kb copy number variant (CNV) at 16p11.2 BP4 and BP5 deletion is flanked by highly homologous blocks of low-copy repeats (Figure 1) and is one of the most frequent etiologies of neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.reference_title: TBX6 null variants and a common hypomorphic allele in congenital scoliosis.
evidence.snippet: A pair of long direct genomic repeats (shown in orange) can mediate 0.6-Mb recurrent deletions.

nodes.description: Satiety regulation is altered before overt obesity in some deletion carriers. The responsible gene-to-circuit pathway remains incompletely resolved.

evidence.snippet: Altered satiety presents prior to the onset of obesity (Maillard et al. 2016), serving as a flag to control portion size.

nodes.description: Neurologist-directed therapy is individualized to the seizure syndrome. Phenobarbital, carbamazepine, and oxcarbazepine showed favorable responses in the retrospective deletion cohort, especially self-limited infantile epilepsy; this was not a randomized drug comparison.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of Seizures and Epilepsy in Individuals With Recurrent Deletions and Duplications in the 16p11.2 Region.
evidence.snippet: Seizures responded favorably to phenobarbital, carbamazepine, and oxcarbazepine in the deletion group, specifically in the Se(F)IE, and to various antiseizure medications in the duplication group.
Taken with the ECHO and European 16p11.2 Consortium cohorts, disinhibited behavior, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and ASD diagnoses were again the most common (20–25%) [8].

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of Seizures and Epilepsy in Individuals With Recurrent Deletions and Duplications in the 16p11.2 Region.
evidence.snippet: Among 129 individuals with the 16p11.2 deletion, 31 (24%) had at least one seizure, including 23 (18%) who met criteria for epilepsy; 42% of them fit the phenotype of classic or atypical Self-limited (Familial) Infantile Epilepsy (Se(F)IE).
Seizures are observed in approximately 25% of individuals with the recurrent deletion.

nodes.description: Individualized speech and language intervention addresses articulation, apraxia, receptive and expressive deficits.

evidence.reference_title: Health supervision for children and adolescents with 16p11.2 deletion syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Evaluation and prompt treatment for speech and language disorders, including expressiveness, receptiveness, apraxia (Mei et al. 2018), auditory feedback, and motor control (Demopoulos et al. 2018), as well as social pragmatic communication disorders (Jiménez-Romero et al. 2022).

nodes.description: A hypomorphic TBX6 allele in trans to the deletion further reduces effective TBX6 dosage. The T-C-A risk haplotype is a documented modifier of congenital scoliosis in deletion carriers.

evidence.reference_title: TBX6 null variants and a common hypomorphic allele in congenital scoliosis.
evidence.snippet: In vitro functional assays suggested that the risk haplotype is a hypomorphic allele.

evidence.reference_title: TBX6 null variants and a common hypomorphic allele in congenital scoliosis.
evidence.snippet: The T-C-A risk haplotype was a significant risk factor for congenital scoliosis in series 3 (5 of 6 persons with congenital scoliosis vs. 5 of 30 persons without scoliosis, P=0.004 by Fisher’s exact test), which further supports the TBX6 compound inheritance model of the disorder.

nodes.description: The deletion removes one TBX6 allele. For congenital scoliosis, the dosage of the remaining allele modifies the effect of this null allele.

evidence.reference_title: TBX6 null variants and a common hypomorphic allele in congenital scoliosis.
evidence.snippet: However, the discordant intrafamilial phenotypes of 16p11.2 deletion carriers suggest that heterozygous TBX6 null mutation is insufficient to cause congenital scoliosis.

We conducted a comprehensive chart review and in person examination by a child neurologist of 136 deletion carriers and identified features including symmetric hypotonia (50%), abnormal agility or clumsiness (47%), tremor (equivalent to essential tremor-25%) and increased reflexes/clonus (13%) in deletion carriers [28].
The most common anomaly is vertebral abnormalities (hemivertebrae or kyphoscoliosis affect ~20% of carriers) [10].

nodes.description: Healthy eating, portion awareness, physical activity, and nutrition follow-up address childhood obesity risk.

evidence.snippet: Because of the high risk of obesity beginning in adolescence, encourage healthy eating habits with attention to portion size and an active lifestyle from a young age.

Clinical follow-up data from adults suggests that the greatest medical challenges are obesity and related comorbidities that can be exacerbated by medications used to treat behavioral and psychiatric problems.
